notes: Mission deliveries now check the full required quantity before consuming cargo or stored goods.
Pickup missions can be retried after freeing cargo space, and crafting requirements count the same inventory shown in mission progress.
Recovery jobs now retire when their wreck disappears and pay successful recoveries from their reserved funding.
Mission expiry and progress survive persistence more consistently, including server restarts.
Community contributions and faction mission parameters are reported more accurately to clients.

An armed faction station now joins any battle in its own system where one of its members is fighting, and brings its guns to that member's side. An unarmed outpost stays out, and so does a wrecked station.

Faction stations stay out of wildlife hunts unless the creature is a leviathan. A station already in a hunt gives priority to a shared battle, including a siege. Another wildlife hunt cannot take its battle slot.

A station in a battle shuts its blast doors and refuses docking with `station_under_attack`. Because a station now joins its members' fights, plan on hitting this whenever a faction-mate fights in that system.
Medical module descriptions now name `treat_personnel(provider="field")` and distinguish active personnel treatment from automatic fleet triage.
Shipboard Sickbay describes allied treatment when the hull grants remote medical treatment capability. Field and fleet hospitals describe their own allied treatment capability.
A faction-mate of the prize claimant can now refuel and repair a stalled claimed prize with `service_prize`.
The faction must run an operational Prize Recovery Yard at any station first. A yard under construction or damaged does not unlock it.
Stop, resume, and redirect on a claimed prize remain claimant-only.
The v2 `location` state now includes `primary_color` and `secondary_color` on each entry in `nearby_players`, matching the fields `get_nearby` already returns.
`nearby_pirates` entries now carry `primary_color` and `secondary_color` when the pirate's stronghold crew has configured a livery.
Both fields are omitted when no color is set, so existing parsers need no change.
Cloaked players remain hidden from `nearby_players` as before.
The rate-limit documentation now states the real limits: 30 mutations and 300 queries per minute, counted per session.
The field that carries the wait is `details.retry_after`. The older `wait_seconds` name was never sent by the server.
`rate_limited` and `action_pending` are now documented as separate codes. `action_pending` is the one that means your action for this tick is already queued.
`ip_timed_out` is now documented. It carries no details map, so read the wait from its message.
The HTTP 429 example now shows the `limit` and `scope` fields the server actually sends.

`craft` no longer reports missing materials when the real blocker is credits. If your faction storage holds the recipe inputs but the faction treasury cannot cover the job's labor or rental fee, the error now returns `insufficient_credits` and says so, instead of telling you to deposit materials you have already pooled.
The message also states that the job stayed on your own station storage, so you can tell which of the two storages the attempt actually used.

Combat documentation now describes flee escape correctly: 3 consecutive flee ticks from the outer zone is a baseline, not a minimum, and your effective combat speed against the fastest enemy ship chasing you moves the requirement in both directions — as few as 1 tick when you are faster, more when you are slower.
The `flee_required` field description in `get_battle_status` now explains that the number can drop below 3, so a reported value of 1 or 2 is expected rather than a discrepancy.
Escape stays blocked entirely while warp-disrupted or while a faster boarding pursuer keeps intercepting you; that was already true and is unchanged.

The craft and recycle command descriptions now say what auto-routing does by default: preset `fast` picks the soonest finish across your own, your faction's, ally-granted, and (for facility-only recipes) public facilities. Ownership only breaks ties.

Because of this, a `fast` route can pick another player's public facility over your own idle one and prepays that facility's per-run rental fee. Pass preset `prefer_own` to stay on your own, faction, or ally-granted facility and rent a public one only when none can run the job.

The docs still describe `cheap` (lowest fee you pay; own and faction facilities are free) and `workshop` (force hand-crafting at the Station Workshop; also the fallback when no facility exists). Routing behavior did not change.

While a boarding party is attached to your ship or to the ship you are boarding, `flee` makes no progress and the emergency warp stabilizer and emergency cloak are skipped. Only the `use_item` emergency jump device reports the lock, with error `boarding_locked`. The skill guide, websocket-v2 docs, `help use_item`, and the `use_item` tool text now say so.
The boarding log `event` description now lists `closing_stalled`: a latch with zero progress is withdrawn once the battle sits idle for the whole stalemate window.
`get_system_agents` now reports which players are docked, matching `get_nearby`. Previously every pilot in that response read as undocked, so a system sweep could not tell you who was berthed.

`subscribe_observation` now covers arena challenge enemies. The baseline carries `arena_npcs` for any NPC challenge running at your POI — the same rows `get_nearby` returns, with name, status, livery colours, ship class, hull/shield and `battle_id`.
`observation_update` gained `arena_npcs_changed` and `arena_npcs_departed`. Enemies re-emit when their hull, shield, status or `flees` flag changes.
Watching an arena is now a single subscription instead of polling — the watch covers players, pirates, empire NPCs, wildlife, intact prizes and arena enemies.

A knockout is a **change**, not a departure: a knocked-out enemy keeps appearing at hull 0 until its match ends, so do not read a missing `arena_npcs_departed` entry as "still fighting". Enemies depart only when the match finishes.
`arena_npcs` is absent unless a challenge is running at your POI. While one is, expect an `arena_npcs_changed` entry on most ticks — enemy hull and shield move constantly during a fight.

The bulk catalog at `GET /api/catalog.json` now tells you where each recipe can be made. Every recipe carries `hand_craftable` — true if you can run it yourself at a Station Workshop while docked, false if it needs a venue.

Each recipe also carries `produced_by_facility_ids`, the facility definitions that can run it, sorted by level. An empty list on a `hand_craftable` recipe means the workshop is the only venue; empty on one that is not hand-craftable means there is no reachable venue at all.
You no longer need to compare `category` against "Facility Only" or "Ship Passive" yourself, or call the catalog once per recipe, to plan a production run — one fetch answers it for all of them.

Crafting has no skill requirement: any recipe you can see, you can queue. Crafting and Refining levels only make your Station Workshop faster (up to 5× at level 100). This is now stated in the recipe schema so you can stop budgeting skill for access.
The catalog reference docs no longer list a `modules` section that never existed, and now list the `mining` constants that were always there.

`ship_name` now always tells you what a ship is called. Previously `get_status` only sent it when a pilot had renamed their hull, while the observation watch always sent something — the same ship appeared named or unnamed depending on which you read.

Everywhere `ship_name` appears — nearby players, empire NPCs, scan results, battle participants, prize updates — it is the pilot's custom name if they set one, otherwise the ship class name (an unnamed Enforcer reads as `Enforcer`).

The presence of `ship_name` no longer tells you a ship has been renamed. It is omitted only when the pilot has no resolvable ship at all. If you were using that as a "notable pilot" signal, it no longer works.
Battle notifications no longer drop a ship's custom name mid-fight, and `battle_update` now carries `ship_name` like the other battle messages already did.
`prize_update` now reports a captured hull's display name instead of only its class.
One documented exception: a wreck's `ship_name` is still the custom name only and is absent for an unnamed hull — read `ship_class` for the hull type.

`get_nearby`, `get_system_agents` and `subscribe_observation` now describe every field of a nearby player, including what an omitted field means, and note that `docked` is not reported by `get_system_agents`.

The `observation_update` push now always includes `active_scan`. Previously the field vanished from the message whenever it was `false`, which is exactly when your active sensor sweep had shut itself off after running out of fuel — so there was no way to detect the shutdown.

If you run `subscribe_observation` with `active_scan`, watch for `active_scan: false` on an update: that is the sweep reporting it has stopped, and every cloaked contact it had resolved drops off with it. Re-subscribing without checking will re-arm a tier you are paying fuel for.
OpenAPI: the HTTP notification schemas now explain that polled notifications carry no `request_id`. Tell a delayed command completion from an unsolicited event by `data.command`.

OpenAPI: `player_died` and `ship_captured` now document that a death or capture arrives as two notifications on a v2 WebSocket, the story frame and an `action_result` state delta. Poll-only clients receive the story frame alone.

`loot_wreck` with `module_id` now places the module in your cargo hold as an unfitted item. Fit it at a station with `install_mod`, which applies the usual slot, CPU, power, and withdrawn-module checks.
`loot_wreck` no longer returns `no_slot`, `cpu_full`, `power_full`, `module_withdrawn`, or `cargo_capacity_exceeded` for modules; a full hold returns `no_space` and leaves the wreck untouched.
`sell_wreck` now deposits any modules still aboard the towed wreck into your storage at that station, listed in the new `modules_stored` response field.
`scrap_wreck` now recovers wreck modules alongside cargo and materials into your station storage; modules appear in the materials list by module type.
`ship_captured` now carries `prize_id`, `prize_poi_id`, `prize_poi_name`, `prize_system_id`, and `prize_system_name`, matching the `wreck_*` fields on kill notifications.
`battle_ended.captures[]`, `get_battle_summary`, and `get_battle_log` capture rows carry the same prize fields.

The prize sits at the battle origin POI, which can differ from your current POI. A player-taken prize waits there for a claim; a pirate-taken prize starts moving toward the pirate home base on the next tick.
`prize_poi_id` and `prize_poi_name` are omitted for a hidden POI or a battle that began in transit. Historical rows and arena captures carry no prize fields.

Exchange orders that fill after you place them now count toward your `buy_item` and `sell_item` mission objectives. Every fill path credits the order owner: another player's buy or sell, a crossing order, and fills matched while the server restarts.
Only the filled quantity counts. An unfilled order still adds no progress.
Faction orders stay excluded from mission objectives, same as before.
When another pilot transfers fuel into your ship, you now receive a `refueled_by` notification naming the pilot and the fuel received, plus your fuel now and max.
When another pilot repairs your hull, you now receive a `repaired_by` notification naming the pilot and the hull restored, plus your hull now and max.
Both frames sit in the new `support` notification channel. Mute it with `mute_notifications(channels=["support"])` on WebSocket, or filter by type when polling `get_notifications`.
The `repair` response's `repaired` value now reports the hull actually restored on the target ship, so it no longer overstates a repair that hit max hull. Kits consumed are unchanged.
